title: STEP files cannot be imported - assimp seems to use randomly incorrect (?) importers

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: Explanation
labels.description: Great discussion / explanation other users can learn from

body:
Library version: master @ cd42b99
Platform: Windows 10 64-bit
Compiler: MSVC 2019 64-bit

STEP files cannot be imported, at least none that I've tried, because the STEP importer (which seems to be the IFC importer in this version) is not used. Instead, other importers are being used, and failing (so far I've observed the X3D, DXF and STL importers). I cannot identify the criteria that determines which importer is used.

A test program is [here](https://github.com/JC3/ModelSplit/tree/assimp-master-cd42b99/specific_tests/x3d_importer_fallback) (does not actually depend on Qt). This program just prints some info about the extension, and also tries to import a file and prints some info about the importer that was used. 

The output (slightly edited for brevity), when run against the model [here](https://github.com/JC3/ModelSplit/tree/assimp-master-cd42b99/specific_tests/x3d_importer_fallback/models) as well as a dummy zero-length file with a .stp extension, is:

```
assimp 5.0.1 (master @ cd42b995)
Extension: "stp"
  IsExtensionSupported:       true
  GetImporterIndex:           39
  GetImporter:                plugin=0x0000015974491640
  ->GetExtensionList:         ifc ifczip stp
  ->GetInfo->mName:           Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) Importer
  ->GetInfo->mFileExtensions: ifc ifczip stp

[created zero-length dummy file: dummy.stp]
  ReadFile (pFlags=0):
    ReadFile:                 success
    importerIndex:            46
    mName:                    Extensible 3D(X3D) Importer
    scene->mFlags:            0x00000000
[deleting dummy file]
---------------------------------------------------------------
[using specified file: models/scene.stp]
  ReadFile (pFlags=0):
    ReadFile:                 error: DXF: no data blocks loaded
    importerIndex:            16
    mName:                    Drawing Interchange Format (DXF) Importer
---------------------------------------------------------------
[using specified file: models/io1-cm-214.stp]
  ReadFile (pFlags=0):
    ReadFile:                 error: Failed to determine STL storage representation for models/io1-cm-214.stp.
    importerIndex:            14
    mName:                    Stereolithography (STL) Importer
---------------------------------------------------------------
[using specified file: models/io1-tu-203.stp]
  ReadFile (pFlags=0):
    ReadFile:                 error: DXF: no data blocks loaded
    importerIndex:            16
    mName:                    Drawing Interchange Format (DXF) Importer
---------------------------------------------------------------
```

With the key bit of code from the test program being:

```
        printf("  ReadFile (pFlags=0):\n");

        Assimp::Importer importer;
        const aiScene *scene;
        if (!(scene = importer.ReadFile(filename, 0)))
            printf("    ReadFile:                 error: %s\n", importer.GetErrorString());
        else
            printf("    ReadFile:                 success\n");

        int index = importer.GetPropertyInteger("importerIndex", -1);
        printf("    importerIndex:            %d\n", index);

        const aiImporterDesc *desc = importer.GetImporterInfo(index);
        printf("    mName:                    %s\n", desc ? desc->mName : "(null info)");
        if (scene)
            printf("    scene->mFlags:            0x%08x\n", scene->mFlags);
```

The interpretation of that output is:

- The library correctly reports that the IFC importer should be handling the ".stp" file extension, but
- A zero-length dummy file named "dummy.stp" got handled by the X3D importer (also note that ReadFile indicated success, which I'm assuming is related to #3786).
- The "scene.stp" file (which I generated with assimp's stp exporter) got handled by the DXF importer.
- The "io1-cm-214.stp" file (an AP214 reference file from [here](https://www.cax-if.org/cax/cax_stepLib.php)) got handled by the STL importer.
- The "io1-tu-203.stp" file (an AP203 reference file from the same place) got handled by the DXF importer.

It almost seems random, but I don't know.

In any case, this is preventing STEP files from being imported. The example files referenced above can be found in the linked test program's directory tree.

This seems to be a regression. In the 5.0.1 Bugfix release from the releases page, the STEP Importer was always used.
